subject: general
question: Which earthquake waves involve transverse displacement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**S - Waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• S-waves, or secondary waves, are a type of seismic wave that move through the body of an object and involve transverse displacement.
 
• Transverse displacement means the particles move perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• S-waves can only move through solid materials and are slower than P-waves (primary waves).
 
• They are responsible for the shaking felt during an earthquake and are typically more destructive than P-waves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **P - Waves**

 
 
• Also known as primary waves, P-waves are the fastest type of seismic wave and the first to be detected by seismographs.
 
• They involve compressional displacement, meaning the particles move back and forth in the same direction as the wave propagation.
 
• P-waves can travel through both solid and liquid materials, including the Earth's core.
 
 
 
• **L - Waves**
 
 
• L-waves, or Love waves, are a type of surface seismic wave that cause horizontal shearing of the ground.
 
• They travel slower than body waves (P and S waves) but are usually more destructive due to their larger amplitude and longer duration.
 
 
 
• **Rayleigh Surface Waves**
 
 
• Rayleigh waves are a type of surface wave that travel along the free surface of solids.
 
• They cause both vertical and horizontal ground movement in a rolling motion, similar to ocean waves.
 
• Rayleigh waves typically cause the most damage during an earthquake.
